{"passages":[{"reference":"20.16","text":"And the father said, “I sinned; I confess it.” Annoubion said, “I too, together with him, ask you to pardon a noble and good old man who was deceived, for the unfortunate man has become the plaything of the notorious fellow. Still, I will tell you how it happened. This good old man came to greet us. At that very hour, all of us who were present there happened to be listening together to Simon, who wanted to flee that night because he had heard that certain men were coming from somewhere, here to Laodicea, under a royal order to search for him. When Faustus entered, Simon, revealing what was in his own mind, spoke to us as follows: ‘When he arrives, have him share salt with you. I will prepare an ointment so that, after dining, taking it, and anointing his own face, he may appear to everyone to have my form. But you, having first been anointed by me with the juices of a certain plant, will not be deceived by his strange form; to everyone else, however, Faustus will appear to be Simon.’”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"παίγνιον γὰρ γέγονεν ὁ δυστυχὴς τοῦ περιβοήτου","chosen":"the unfortunate man has become the plaything of the notorious fellow","rationale":"Preserves the image of Faustus as another person’s plaything and the substantival force of περιβοήτου without inserting Simon’s name."},{"source_quote":"ἀκηκοὼς ἐπιδημήσειν ποθέν τινας ἐνταῦθα τῇ Λαοδικείᾳ","chosen":"because he had heard that certain men were coming from somewhere, here to Laodicea","rationale":"ποθέν means “from somewhere,” while ἐνταῦθα and τῇ Λαοδικείᾳ locate their expected arrival."},{"source_quote":"τὸν ἴδιον θυμὸν φήσας","chosen":"revealing what was in his own mind","rationale":"θυμός can refer to an inward impulse, disposition, intention, or anger. The ensuing disclosure favors the broader contextual rendering without excluding its forceful emotional nuance."},{"source_quote":"Ἁλῶν αὐτὸν ἐλθόντα συμμετασχεῖν ὑμῖν ποιήσατε","chosen":"When he arrives, have him share salt with you","rationale":"Ἁλῶν is defensibly the genitive plural of ἅλς, “salt,” as the object of συμμετασχεῖν. Sharing salt depicts participation in the meal; no correction to the printed reading is required."},{"source_quote":"μύρον τι","chosen":"an ointment","rationale":"μύρον denotes perfumed oil or ointment, and the subsequent anointing supports “ointment.”"},{"source_quote":"δειπνήσας καὶ ἀναλαβὼν τὸ ἴδιον χρίσας πρόσωπον","chosen":"after dining, taking it, and anointing his own face","rationale":"The ointment is understood as the object taken, while τὸ ἴδιον ... πρόσωπον is read together despite the intervening participle."},{"source_quote":"τῆς ξένης αὐτοῦ μορφῆς","chosen":"his strange form","rationale":"ξένης describes the transformed appearance as strange, foreign, or unfamiliar to the observers."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"20.17","text":"While he was setting these things forth, I said, “What benefit do you now gain from such a scheme?” Simon said, “First, those who are searching for me will seize him and then cease their search against me. And even if he should be killed by the royal hand, his children—who abandoned me, prosphygont........., and are working together—will experience the greatest grief.”

“For now, Peter, I confess the truth to you: I was afraid of the .........stō—to disclose this. But Simon did not even give us time to speak privately ..........mōn to him; as for Simon’s evil counsel—it appeared. At any rate, in the middle of the night Simon got up and fled toward Judea, escorted by both Appion and Athenodorus. I then pretended that my body was unwell so that, by remaining behind after they had left, I might make him return at once to his own home, in case he might be able to escape notice while hiding among you, lest he be seized as Simon by those searching for Simon and die under the royal wrath. I therefore sent him away to you at an unseasonable hour, and out of concern for him I came by night both to see him and to leave very quickly, before those who sent....................., having returned.”

Then, looking at us, he said, “I, Annoubion, see your father’s true form, being one who has been anointed by Simon himself—I gave this account beforehand—so that the true form of Faustus might appear to my eyes. Being utterly astounded, therefore, I marvel at Simon’s magic: though you are standing here, you do not recognize your own father.” As the father, the mother, and we ourselves wept over the misfortune common to us all, Annoubion also sympathized with us and shed tears.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ὑπὸ βασιλικῆς χειρὸς ἀναιρεθείη","chosen":"should be killed by the royal hand","rationale":"Preserves the source’s personifying image of the royal hand rather than reducing it to an abstract governmental authority."},{"source_quote":"τὴν ἐπὶ Ἰουδαίαν ἐποιεῖτο φυγήν","chosen":"fled toward Judea","rationale":"ἐπί with the accusative marks the direction of Simon’s flight."},{"source_quote":"ἐπὶ τὰ ἑαυτοῦ ἐπανελθεῖν","chosen":"return at once to his own home","rationale":"The idiom can refer to one’s home, possessions, affairs, or people. Faustus’s return to his family makes “home” contextually suitable, though the expression itself is broader."},{"source_quote":"ἀωρίας","chosen":"at an unseasonable hour","rationale":"The adverbial genitive denotes action at an unusually late, early, or otherwise inconvenient hour."},{"source_quote":"ἐναλειψάμενος ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ τοῦ Σίμωνος ὢν προδιηγησάμην","chosen":"being one who has been anointed by Simon himself—I gave this account beforehand","rationale":"ὢν is translated as a nominative participle agreeing with the speaker. προδιηγησάμην is treated parenthetically; alternatively, the participles may be attached differently within the interrupted sentence."},{"source_quote":"ὅτι ἑστῶτες τὸν ὑμέτερον οὐ γνωρίζετε πατέρα","chosen":"though you are standing here, you do not recognize your own father","rationale":"The participle ἑστῶτες is retained and understood concessively; a more mechanically circumstantial rendering would be “standing here, you do not recognize.”"}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"οἵτινες ἐμὲ καταλιπόντες προσφυγόντ......... συνεργοῦσι","issue":"The selected edition prints nine dots after the surviving incomplete form προσφυγόντ. Its lexical stem suggests seeking or taking refuge, but its completion and the missing intervening wording are unavailable. The translation retains the transliterated fragment and exactly nine dots without restoration.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"ἐφοβούμην τὸν .........στω τοῦτο μηνύειν","issue":"The selected edition prints nine dots between the accusative article τὸν and the incomplete surviving fragment στω. The gap prevents determination of their relationship to one another and to μηνύειν. The translation therefore preserves the article, gap, and fragment without identifying the missing person or changing τὸν.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"ἀλλ’ οὐδὲ καιρὸν ἡμῖν ὁ Σίμων ἐδίδου πρὸς τὸ ἰδιάζειν .......... μῶν αὐτῷ τὴν ἐκ τοῦ Σίμωνος κακὴν ἐφάνη βουλήν","issue":"Ten printed dots interrupt the sentence and are followed by the incomplete fragment μῶν. The surviving accusative phrase τὴν ... κακὴν ... βουλήν does not straightforwardly function as the subject of ἐφάνη. The English presents the wording as an anacoluthic, detached fragment rather than silently changing the accusative to a nominative; the missing connection remains unavailable.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"πρὶν τοὺς πέμψαντας ..................... ἐπανελθών","issue":"The selected edition prints twenty-one dots. The lost material prevents determination of how τοὺς πέμψαντας and the nominative participle ἐπανελθών were connected. The exact gap and surviving syntactic fragments are retained without restoration.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"20.18","text":"Then Peter promised us that our father’s form would be restored. He said to him, “You have heard, Faustus, about our circumstances. Therefore, when the deceptive form laid upon you becomes useful to us and you assist us in the matters we command, then I too will restore your true form to you, after you have first done what I tell you.”

The father said, “Anything that is possible for me I will do with the greatest eagerness; only restore my form to my own people.” Peter answered, “You yourself heard with your own ears from my advance messengers, who came from Antioch and said that Simon had been there and had vehemently incited the crowds against me, calling me a magician, a murderer, a deceiver, and a sorcerer—to such an extent that everyone there longs to taste my flesh. You will therefore do as I say: leave Clement with me and go ahead of us to Antioch with your wife and also with your sons Faustinus and Faustinianus. Certain others will accompany you as well, whom I judge capable of serving my purpose.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τῆς τοῦ πατρὸς μορφῆς τὴν ἀποκατάστασιν","chosen":"that our father’s form would be restored","rationale":"ἀποκατάστασις denotes restoration to a former condition, here explicitly the father’s appearance."},{"source_quote":"ἡ περικειμένη σοι πλάνος μορφὴ","chosen":"the deceptive form laid upon you","rationale":"περίκειμαι presents the form as something placed around or upon Faustus, while πλάνος characterizes it as deceptive."},{"source_quote":"τῶν προόδων μου","chosen":"my advance messengers","rationale":"The substantival plural refers to people sent ahead of Peter; “forerunners” is another possible rendering."},{"source_quote":"τῶν ἐμῶν ἀπογεύσασθαι σαρκῶν","chosen":"to taste my flesh","rationale":"Preserves the violent bodily image rather than generalizing it as a desire merely to kill Peter; the Greek uses the plural σαρκῶν."},{"source_quote":"προαγαγὼν ἡμᾶς εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν","chosen":"go ahead of us to Antioch","rationale":"The following narrative has Faustus reach Antioch before Peter and later notify him. Formally, προάγω with an object can also mean “lead us onward.”"},{"source_quote":"ὑπουργῆσαι τῷ ἐμῷ θελήματι","chosen":"serving my purpose","rationale":"θέλημα denotes Peter’s will or intended purpose here, and ὑπουργέω denotes rendering practical assistance."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"20.19","text":"“With these people, in Antioch ....... while you appear as Simon, publicly proclaim your own meta........: ‘I, Simon, proclaim these things to you. I confess: unjustly I katapseu........ is a deceiver, not a murderer, not a sorcerer, nor is he any of the vile things I previously went so far as to say about him while driven by anger. I beg you—I myself, who brought upon him the hatred among you—stop hating him. For he is a true apostle of the true prophet sent by God for the salvation of the world. Therefore I myself also advise you to obey him concerning what he proclaims, since your entire city will be utterly destroyed. I want you to know the reason why I have confessed these things to you. This very night, angels of God were severely scourging me, the impious man, as an enemy of the herald of truth. Therefore I appeal to you: even if I myself should come on another occasion and speak while making an attempt against Peter, do not accept me. For I confess openly to you: I am a magician, I am a deceiver, I am a sorcerer. For perhaps it is possible through reorientation to put away the sins previously committed by me.’”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ἐν ὅσῳ ὡς Σίμων φαίνῃ","chosen":"while you appear as Simon","rationale":"ἐν ὅσῳ gives the period during which Faustus visibly bears Simon’s form."},{"source_quote":"οὐ μιαιφόνος","chosen":"not a murderer","rationale":"μιαιφόνος evokes bloodshed and blood-pollution and functions here as an accusation of murderous violence."},{"source_quote":"ὅσα ποτὲ φαῦλα περὶ αὐτοῦ λέγων ἔφθανον","chosen":"any of the vile things I previously went so far as to say about him","rationale":"φθάνω with the participle can convey previously or anticipatorily doing something, or going so far as to do it. “Previously hastened to say” is also possible."},{"source_quote":"αὐτὸς ἐγὼ ὁ τοῦ πρὸς ὑμᾶς μίσους αἴτιος αὐτῷ γεγονώς","chosen":"I myself, who brought upon him the hatred among you","rationale":"The context favors taking πρὸς ὑμᾶς as locating the hatred among or in relation to the listeners and αὐτῷ as marking Peter as the affected person. A more directional reading, “the hatred toward you,” is grammatically possible, but its relationship to αὐτῷ would remain uncertain."},{"source_quote":"ἄγγελοί με τοῦ θεοῦ τὸν ἀσεβῆ ... δεινῶς ἐμαστίγουν","chosen":"angels of God were severely scourging me, the impious man","rationale":"Retains the appositional accusation τὸν ἀσεβῆ and the continuing force of the imperfect verb."},{"source_quote":"μετανοίᾳ","chosen":"through reorientation","rationale":"The term denotes moral redirection in this context and does not itself specify an added destination."},{"source_quote":"ἀπολῦσαι τὰ προπεπραγμένα μοι ἁμαρτήματα","chosen":"to put away the sins previously committed by me","rationale":"ἀπολύω can mean release, dismiss, or put away. The construction permits a nuance of either removing the sins or obtaining release from them."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"μετὰ τούτων ἐν τῇ Ἀντιοχείᾳ ....... ἐν ὅσῳ","issue":"The selected edition prints seven dots after Ἀντιοχείᾳ. The unavailable predicate or connective has not been restored, and the translation retains exactly seven dots.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"δημοσίᾳ κήρυξον τὴν σεαυτοῦ μετα ........","issue":"Only the incomplete fragment μετα survives before the eight printed dots. The identity, completion, and meaning of the noun are unavailable. The translation therefore retains the fragment as “meta” followed by exactly eight dots rather than supplying “change,” “reorientation,” or another completed noun.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"ὁμολογῶ ἀδίκως καταψεύ ........ ἔστι πλάνος, οὐ μιαιφόνος, οὐ γόης","issue":"The selected edition prints eight dots after the incomplete verbal form καταψεύ. Its completion, object, and any further words are unavailable, so the fragment is transliterated and the gap remains explicit. The surviving clause is ἔστι πλάνος, without a printed negation; the translation therefore preserves “is a deceiver.” Any qualification or negation that might once have stood in the gap has not been restored.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"20.20","text":"As Peter was giving these instructions, the father said, “I know what you want, so do not weary yourself. For when I get there, I will take no less care to say what ought to be said about you.” Peter again instructed him, “When you perceive that the city has turned from its hatred and now desires to see us, send word and inform me, and we will catch up with you there. When I arrive there, on that very day I will drive away your alien form and make your own form appear unmistakably to your people and to everyone else.”

After saying this, he arranged for the sons, my brothers, to accompany him, and he commanded our mother Mattidia and some of the more loyal people to go with him. But the mother regarded going with him reluctantly. “For I appear to be an adulteress while consorting with Simon’s form. If I am indeed compelled to go with him, it is impossible to recline on the same couch with him. And I do not know whether I will be persuaded even to go with him.”

When she hesitated to leave, Annoubion encouraged her and said, “Believe me and Peter, and also the very voice, that .... is your husband, whom I love no less than you do. And I myself, for him, sym.........” When Annoubion had said this, the mother promised to go with him.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"διὸ μὴ κάμνε","chosen":"so do not weary yourself","rationale":"κάμνω can mean grow weary or exert oneself laboriously; the father indicates that Peter need not labor over further explanation."},{"source_quote":"τὴν πόλιν μεταβαλομένην τοῦ μίσους","chosen":"the city has turned from its hatred","rationale":"The genitive τοῦ μίσους is taken as the state from which the city changes. “Changed with respect to its hatred” is also grammatically possible but less directly contrasts with its new desire to see Peter."},{"source_quote":"αὐτόθι ἐπικαταληψόμεθά σε","chosen":"we will catch up with you there","rationale":"ἐπικαταλαμβάνω here denotes overtaking or joining Faustus after he has gone ahead."},{"source_quote":"ἀπλανῶς φαίνεσθαι","chosen":"appear unmistakably","rationale":"The adverb means without deception or mistake, reversing the deceptive appearance imposed by Simon."},{"source_quote":"τῶν γνησιωτέρων τινὰς","chosen":"some of the more loyal people","rationale":"The substantival comparative can describe more genuine, trustworthy, or devoted associates. “More genuine ones” is a more formally transparent alternative."},{"source_quote":"Μοιχὰς γὰρ εἶναι δοκῶ τῇ Σίμωνος συνοῦσα μορφῇ","chosen":"For I appear to be an adulteress while consorting with Simon’s form","rationale":"δοκῶ may mean “I appear” or “I consider myself.” The context emphasizes the adulterous appearance created by accompanying someone who visibly bears Simon’s form."},{"source_quote":"ἐπὶ τῆς αὐτῆς κλίνης συγκατακλιθήσεσθαι","chosen":"to recline on the same couch with him","rationale":"κλίνη may denote a couch or bed; the literal posture is retained while the marital implication remains contextual."},{"source_quote":"ὃν οὐκ ἔλαττόν σου ἀγαπῶ","chosen":"whom I love no less than you do","rationale":"The reassurance favors comparing Annoubion’s love for the husband with Mattidia’s love for him. The elliptical comparison can alternatively mean “whom I love no less than I love you.”"}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"αὐτῇ δὲ τῇ φωνῇ ὅτι .... ἐστὶν ὁ σὸς σύμβιος","issue":"The selected edition prints four dots where wording identifying the husband would be expected. The context may suggest a demonstrative, but no restoration has been supplied; the translation retains exactly four dots.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"καὶ αὐτὸς αὐτῷ συμ.........","issue":"The edition preserves καὶ αὐτός, the dative αὐτῷ, and only the incomplete prefix συμ- before nine printed dots. The missing verb, its tense, and the resulting claim are unavailable; the prefix could belong to a compound expressing accompaniment, assistance, sympathy, agreement, or another relationship. The translation retains “I myself,” represents αὐτῷ provisionally as “for him,” and leaves “sym” followed by exactly nine dots without inventing a predicate.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]}]}
